limitations: Operators could not be identified: no approximate mast sites were found within 10 km in our data. This is not the same as no coverage: crowd-sourced site data is incomplete; check the address on Ofcom's mobile coverage checker.
Mast site locations are approximate and incomplete; Ofcom coverage figures are area-level, not exact for this address.
Causes are inferred from public data, not confirmed: operators' network data is not public.
Ookla speeds are quarterly aggregates with no time-of-day detail; congestion can only be inferred.
No address-level Ofcom coverage; Ofcom figures are for the whole constituency and are predictions.
Mast sites are approximate (crowd-sourced OpenCelliD, OpenStreetMap, Ofcom's licence register) and incomplete, so 'no sites found' is weak evidence.
Line of sight uses a surface model (trees and buildings included) and mostly assumed antenna heights; blocked means a weaker signal, not no signal.

The belief is well-supported: there are no speed tests at the point or in the cell [speed_1km][speed_cell] and no confirmed mast sites nearby [nearest_site], so the evidence genuinely cannot distinguish distance from other causes.
